simple.meaning: לֵחַ (lêach) is a Hebrew word meaning “freshness , i.e. vigor.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This word has limited occurrence data, so BibleIQ begins with the Hebrew word, its basic meaning, and the verse where it appears.

simple.summary: לֵחַ (lêach) / H3893 is traced through Deuteronomy 34:7 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H3893. leach [ לֵחַ ] noun masculine moisture, freshness (i.e. force, vigour ); — suffix לֵחהֹ נָס וְלֹא Deut 34:7 and his freshness had not fled ; read probably also בְּלֵחוֺ for בְּלַחְמוֺ ᵑ0 Jer 11:19 (see לֶחֶם near the end; on Zeph 1:17 see לְחוּם ). לֶ֑חִי לְחִי, see לחה .

occurrences.englishText: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died. His eye was not dim, nor his strength gone.
